question: Why does the doubling-time rule use 72 when the exact constant is nearer 69?
answer: Because 72 fits real rates and divides by 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 12. Exact doubling takes 0.693 divided by the natural logarithm of 1 + r years. At 8% that is 9.006 years, and 72 / 8 gives 9.
move: Choose a rule that fits your head as well as your data.
reference: Kellison, The Theory of Interest, 3rd edition, McGraw-Hill, 2009
